modules.title: Air Ambulance Service — Minimum Requirements (Checklist)
modules.notes: This section is the manual's own explicit checklist, organised into five numbered inspection areas: 1 Management and Administration, 2 Aviation Regulations Compliance, 3 Patient Handling Equipment, 4 Flight Crew Qualifications and Fitness, 5 Facilities. Each area is a table with the item number, the checklist question/requirement, a 'REQUIRES ACTION' column with YES/NO tick boxes, and a 'COMMENT/FINDING' free-text column — note the distinct response semantics: the YES/NO records whether the item REQUIRES ACTION (i.e. YES = deficiency found), not whether the requirement is met; the COMMENT/FINDING column captures the inspector's finding. This is mapped to responseType STATUS for every item. Each area's preamble states: 'The following checklist items are provided for guidance and should be used during the Inspection.' Area 3 (Patient Handling Equipment) additionally states: 'This is a minimum requirement list.' The manual's own item numbers are preserved in sourceItemNumber; AAM-### codes are additional stable codes, not replacements. Page 70 numbers two consecutive items '1-04' (quality assurance program, and AHPCZ registered practitioner in-charge) before continuing at 1-05 — this duplicate numbering is preserved as printed and flagged reviewRequired on the second occurrence. Item 1-09 cross-references Inspection Area 5 and item 2-02 cross-references item 1-07; both cross-references are kept verbatim inside the requirement text.

items.requirement: Does the management include a qualified Pilot?
Does the management have an operations office in Zimbabwe?
Does the service have a documented disaster responsiveness procedure?
Does the service have a quality assurance program in place?
Does the service have an AHPCZ registered practitioner in-charge in their decision making structure?
items.reviewReason: Duplicate item number in the manual: page 70 numbers both 'Does the service have a quality assurance program in place?' and this item as '1-04', then continues at 1-05. Both items are preserved with the numbering as printed.

items.requirement: Does the practitioner in charge hold a current practicing certificate issued by the AHPCZ?
Does the practitioner in charge, and all personnel who conduct direct aeromedical work, understand, read, write, and fluently speak English?
Does the service own the aircraft or aircrafts to be used as an air ambulance, if not do they have a current lease agreement or memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the owner?
items.alternatives: If the service does not own the aircraft, a current lease agreement or memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the owner is accepted.

items.requirement: Does the service have a local authority certificate for the premises authorizing use for medical service activities?

items.conditional: If the operator does not have an HPA certificate, the manual directs the inspector to Inspection Area 5 (Facilities).
items.requirement: Does the operator have an HPA certificate, if not see Area 5 below.
Has the service been properly issued with a Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe (CAAZ) aviation operator's certificate (AOC)?
Is the AOC current and in the name of the service provider? (See 1-07)
Does the service or operator's AOC allow for or specify air ambulance work in Zimbabwe?
Does the operator have CAAZ issued airport access passes?
Are the vehicles, including ambulances, issued with airport access passes?
Do all drivers gaining access onto the apron/tarmac have permission from CAAZ, for ramp safety?
A defibrillator equipped with pacing and cardioversion capabilities.
Electronic multi parameter vital signs monitor, ECG, SPO2, RR, NIBP etc.
Manual BP monitor, aneroid.
Thermometer, electronic.
Transport ventilator, Adult, IPPV, SIMV.
Transport ventilator, Paediatric (if 3-05 has no paediatric mode).
items.applicability: Required only if the adult transport ventilator (item 3-05) has no paediatric mode.

items.requirement: Advanced Air Management Kit — laryngoscope, BVM, ETTs, suction, OPAs, NPAs, chest drains (one way flutter valves).
Trauma Management Kit — motion restrict kit, splints, vacuum mattress.
IV management Kit — IV fluids, infusion sets, infusion pumps.
Child Delivery and infant management Kit — cord clamps, towels, pr. scissor.
Oxygen and oxygen delivery equipment.
Dressings and haemorrhage control kit.
Baby incubator.
Patient stretcher with straps.
Emergency and resuscitation drugs.
Burns management kit.
Linen Kit.
Double lock Dangerous Drugs Cupboard, e.g. Morphine, Fentanyl, Pethidine etc.
Refrigerator for drugs at Base and portable cooling container.

items.quantity: a minimum of two pilots approved by CAAZ for the aircraft
items.requirement: A minimum of two pilots approved by CAAZ for the aircraft where the service operates day light flights only.
items.applicability: Where the service operates day light flights only.

items.quantity: a minimum of 4 pilots approved by CAAZ
items.requirement: A minimum of 4 pilots approved by CAAZ where the service is engaged in a twenty four hour day and night operation.
items.applicability: Where the service is engaged in a twenty four hour day and night operation.

items.quantity: a minimum of one flight Doctor
items.requirement: A minimum of one flight Doctor holding an Aviation Health Care Provider's certificate and a valid ACLS certificate.
The doctor must be registered with MDPCZ and has an OPC.

items.quantity: a minimum of one flight nurse or flight medic
items.requirement: A minimum of one flight nurse or flight medic registered with AHPCZ.
The flight Nurse or flight medic holds a post basic qualification in critical patient care and Aviation health care provider certificate.
Current medical fitness test certificate for all crew members.
Does the service employ a CAAZ rated Flight operations officer?
Does the service have a control centre with ground to air communication equipment — e.g. VHF radio, maps, (tracking systems), satellite phone, other telephones?
Is the control centre separated from human traffic for privacy and confidentiality?
Does the service provide rest rooms for males and for females with beds and linen for twenty-four-hour service?
Does the service provide staff catering facilities at their premises?
Does the service have separate ablution facilities for males and females at the premises?
Does the service have a medical waste disposal / management system in place?
Does the service have an approved sluicing facility on site (sluice area)?
